rationale: Author-of-record review of 68ede240 (bead worktree, byte-identical before/after; go build + full `go test ./... -short` green from the worktree). The bead delivers plan §Bead 5 steps 1-5 plus both windows of the written scope extension, and the delivery quality is high: emitInstruct's indeterminate-vs-idle split covers nil-ctx/DerivationFailed/empty-phase before any idle finalization; run.go covers BOTH arrival points (protected-checkout fast path and the no-context fallback) with handleIdleOrDraft/handleIndeterminate; the AC-4b seam matches the plan's decided shape exactly (completeFetchChildrenFn house pattern, advanceState `(mode, nextBead, err)`, early return before step-6.5 so the sync write is structurally skipped); the total cobra classification is real and bidirectional (73 runnable commands, function-pointer-verified aliases, staleness reverse check); the pin-inventory claim VERIFIED (agreement_table_test.go and lifecycle-modes.md diffs are Notes/comment-only, no cell MODE changed; ratchet census 14->15 matches exactly the one new termsafe-classified indeterminate.md interpolation). Disclosure A is acceptable: beadsDirMissing is a filesystem check (never bd error text), and I traced the full uninitialized-workspace path — DiscoverDraftSpecsWithCache short-circuits with zero candidates (specs dir tolerated missing, no bd call), so a no-.beads workspace renders honest idle end-to-end, exactly the regression the guard claims to prevent. Disclosure B is acceptable: minimal unexported seam + stable-name wrapper, restored via t.Cleanup, the house completeMergeMetadataFn pattern. Disclosure C is acceptable: the OLD assertion's real protection (no crash on mode-resolution failure — Run returns nil, no 'loading template' leak) is preserved verbatim in the renamed test; only the dishonest idle-heading expectation flipped, which is R2.3's point. The ModePlan rewording is TRUE for both surviving triggers, verified against DerivePhaseFromChildren: the empty-lifecycle-subset return (derive.go:420) has zero lifecycle beads, and the final all-open fallthrough (derive.go:441) fires only when lifecycleInProgress==0 and lifecycleClosed==0 — no lifecycle work started in either. Two findings block APPROVE. (1) The diff's own claim 'Phase's historical fallback VALUES are unchanged for existing callers' is FALSE for the WorktreeSpec error arms: old code back-filled ModeSpec on a bd/phase-derivation failure; new code leaves Phase empty when DerivationFailed — and internal/cleanup's unforced destructive guard (cleanup.go:50, `ctx.Phase != ModeIdle && ctx.Phase != ""`) keys on exactly that value, so `mindspec cleanup <spec>` from a spec worktree under a bd outage now DELETES the worktree+branch where it previously refused ('still active'). Undisclosed value change with a destructive-direction consequence, contradicting the field's own doc comment; the value change was not even needed — emitInstruct and run.go both check DerivationFailed BEFORE Phase. (2) Disclosure D's dichotomy (real bd+database OR new exported out-of-scope seams) omits a third, house-precedented option: a scripted fake `bd` executable prepended to PATH — cmd/mindspec/next_ready_gate_test.go, the SAME package, already writes fake bd scripts to t.TempDir() and prepends PATH. next's and impl adopt's bd interactions all reach bd via subprocess (runBDFn/bead.RunBDCombined/bead.GetMetadata), so a canned-JSON fake bd plus the now-existing newExecutorFn seam can drive both real RunE paths hermetically with no out-of-scope file edits — AC-14's letter ('asserting EACH prints its result summary before any guidance output on success') is therefore achievable in-bead and currently unmet for 2 of 9 verbs. Minor: FormatResult's new indeterminate summary line prints IndeterminateReason raw while the tail template routes the SAME string through termsafe (the ratchet test itself classifies it termsafe because it may embed agent-writable IDs/paths) — the summary line should get termsafe.Escape (ADR-0042 consistency); and root.go's newExecutorFn comment plus withMockNewExecutor's comment both claim next/impl adopt are driven via the seam, contradicting the Deviations note.
concrete_changes_required: internal/phase/derive.go WorktreeSpec arms: restore the historical fallback VALUE so the claim 'additive, values unchanged' is actually true — on the DerivePhaseWithCache error arm and the AllEpics-probe failure arm, set ctx.Phase = state.ModeSpec alongside DerivationFailed=true (drop the `&& !ctx.DerivationFailed` guard on the ModeSpec back-fill). emitInstruct and run.go check DerivationFailed before Phase, so indeterminate rendering is unaffected; this restores internal/cleanup's (cleanup.go:50) refusal of unforced destructive cleanup under a bd outage. Alternative (also acceptable, if the empty-Phase design is deliberately kept): make cleanup.Run refuse when ctx.DerivationFailed and correct the commit/field-comment claim — but pick one; the current state changes a destructive guard silently.

AC-14 next + impl adopt rows: drive both verbs' real RunE result-before-guidance ordering using the in-package fake-bd-on-PATH pattern (cmd/mindspec/next_ready_gate_test.go precedent: write a canned-JSON `bd` script to t.TempDir(), prepend PATH, restore via t.Cleanup) combined with the newExecutorFn MockExecutor seam — no out-of-scope files, no new exported seams, no real bd. If the panel/tally instead accepts the documented limitation, TestVerbOutput_NextAndImplAdopt_ScopeLimitation's comment must at minimum acknowledge and refute the fake-bd option its current 'no reachable seams' dichotomy omits.

internal/complete/complete.go FormatResult: route r.IndeterminateReason through termsafe.Escape in the 'cannot determine mode: %s' summary line, matching the classification ratchet_template_test.go itself assigns the identical string in the tail template (ADR-0042).

cmd/mindspec/root.go newExecutorFn comment and verb_output_test.go withMockNewExecutor comment: drop 'next' and 'impl adopt' from the driven-verbs list (root.go) and 'impl adopt' (helper comment) — both currently contradict the Deviations report; if change 2 lands, update in the opposite direction instead.

findings.title: WorktreeSpec Phase fallback value silently changed (ModeSpec -> empty), contradicting the disclosed additive-only claim and weakening cleanup's destructive guard
findings.detail: Old ResolveContextFromDirWithCache back-filled ctx.Phase = state.ModeSpec whenever the WorktreeSpec arms hit a bd failure (the `if ctx.Phase == ""` back-fill ran unconditionally); the new `&& !ctx.DerivationFailed` guard leaves Phase empty on those arms. The commit message, BRIEF, and the DerivationFailed field's own doc comment all claim fallback VALUES are unchanged for existing callers — true for WorktreeBead (ModeImplement kept) and WorktreeMain, false for WorktreeSpec. Concrete consumer consequence: internal/cleanup/cleanup.go:49-52 guards unforced worktree+branch deletion with `ctx.Phase != state.ModeIdle && ctx.Phase != ""`; invoked from a spec worktree with bd/Dolt down, the old fabricated ModeSpec tripped the 'still active' refusal (accidentally safe), the new empty Phase passes the guard and exec.Cleanup deletes the worktree and branch without verifying the spec is inactive. No test pinned either behavior, so the suite stayed green through the change.

findings.title: Disclosure D: AC-14's letter unmet for next/impl adopt, and the claimed impossibility omits the in-package fake-bd-on-PATH precedent
findings.detail: The scope-limitation rationale is a two-option dichotomy (real bd binary+database, or new exported seams in out-of-scope packages), and both prongs were verified accurate as stated (internal/next exports no Set*ForTest; adopt's seams are package-private). But cmd/mindspec/next_ready_gate_test.go — the same package as verb_output_test.go — already writes fake `bd` executables into t.TempDir() and prepends them to PATH (installMetadataFailingBD and two sibling helpers). Since every bd interaction on both verbs' success paths is a subprocess exec, a fully canned fake bd (no real bd dependency) plus the newly added newExecutorFn seam can drive nextCmd.RunE and implAdoptCmd.RunE hermetically in-scope. AC-14's text requires the table to assert result-before-guidance for EVERY verb in R2.1's list; 7 of 9 are driven, and the limitation for the other 2 is not forced. The fallback documentation test itself is thin (asserts only RunE non-nil), leaning on the classification gate for red-if-removed.

findings.title: FormatResult's indeterminate summary line bypasses termsafe for the same string the tail escapes
findings.detail: internal/complete/complete.go FormatResult writes `cannot determine mode: %s` with the raw IndeterminateReason (a bd/git error chain), while templates/indeterminate.md renders the identical reason through {{termsafe .IndeterminateReason}} — and the bead's own ratchet_template_test.go entry classifies it classTermsafeText because it 'may embed agent-writable IDs/paths'. The stdout summary deserves the same ADR-0042 treatment (termsafe.Escape), which the impl prompt's shared-helpers section mandated for new message text.

findings.title: Seam comments overstate the driven-verb set
findings.detail: cmd/mindspec/root.go's newExecutorFn comment says the table 'drives spec create/approve, plan approve, next, complete, and impl approve/adopt's REAL RunE functions', and withMockNewExecutor's comment includes 'impl adopt' — both contradict the Deviations report and the actual test set (next and impl adopt are documented, not driven). In a bead whose theme is claim honesty, the comments should match the delivery.

findings.title: Disclosures A, B, C verified acceptable; ModePlan rewording true for both triggers; pin-inventory claim verified
findings.detail: A: beadsDirMissing is filesystem-checked, mirrors bead.Preflight's precondition, and the full uninitialized-workspace path (derivation -> honest idle -> draft scan short-circuits with zero candidates, no bd call) renders idle end-to-end. B: minimal unexported seam + stable wrapper, t.Cleanup-restored, house pattern. C: the old test's real protection — no crash / no 'loading template' leak on mode-resolution failure, Run returning nil — is preserved in the renamed test; only the pre-bead-5 dishonest idle expectation flipped. ModePlan: verified against DerivePhaseFromChildren — the empty-lifecycle-subset return and the all-open fallthrough (lifecycleInProgress==0, lifecycleClosed==0) both make 'No lifecycle work has started yet' true; 'Remaining beads are blocked' was true for neither. Pin inventory: agreement_table_test.go and lifecycle-modes.md changes are Notes/comment prose only, no cell MODE changed; the 14->15 census bump corresponds exactly to indeterminate.md's single new interpolation. AC-4's two-branch test runs over the real completeTail wiring with mutual exclusivity asserted in each branch's own driving case, per round-2 G11.
